rv.q: The honesty of the acting is so enlivening that I'm tempted to rank this production among the very best Wilson revivals I've seen.
When A Noise Within and their masterful production standards mixes with playwright August Wilson’s compelling narrative and director Gregg T. Daniel’s congruous vision, the result is magic.
It is difficult to imagine this play being done any better.

Gilbert has to make Levee be magnetic enough that we understand his faith in himself and exhausting enough that we understand why the other musicians tire of hearing about it. He keeps both qualities alive.

My mind may have wandered during the second half of Act One of August Wilson's Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom, but when all is said and done, it’s a pretty darn spectacular season opener for A Noise Within.
